tagline: A mile inland from the oldest ferry still running.
intro: Off the ferry from Rocky Hill, Route 160 runs a mile inland across the Great Meadows of South Glastonbury and stops being scenic at Roaring Brook. That is the whole of it.

The crossing began in 1655, before there was a Glastonbury or a Rocky Hill, when both were still part of Wethersfield, and it is believed to be the oldest ferry in the country running without a break. It started as a raft poled across, went over to a horse on a treadmill, and took to steam in 1876. Glastonbury built ships along this river in the 18th and early 19th centuries.

moments.title: Rocky Hill-Glastonbury Ferry
moments.text: The Hollister III, a barge for three cars, goes over in tow of the diesel towboat Cumberland, and the ferry turns up in Billy Joel's video for "The River of Dreams".

moments.title: Great Meadows
moments.text: The farm fields here still keep the land-use patterns of the 17th century, with Colonial and Greek Revival farmhouses among them.

practical: The ferry is seasonal and does not run in winter.
